meta.title: dsh-genui — Replies become interfaces.
meta.description: dsh-genui turns DeepSeek Harness replies into real interfaces: one dsh-ui fence renders sortable tables, draggable charts and self-grading quizzes in the browser.
hero.ledeAfter: fence turns a reply into sortable tables, draggable charts and quizzes you can answer.
hero.demoP1: 18 tasks shipped, 2 slipped. Average cycle 3.4 days, 0.6 faster than last week.
hero.demoP2: By team: frontend 8, backend 6, design 4. Payments integration slipped two days — the only risk this week.
hero.panelCaption: Rendered by the real runtime — not a screenshot
manifesto.p1: A fence inside the reply is plain JSON. Its fields decide whether it becomes a table, a chart or a quiz — the renderer validates, repairs and draws real components.
manifesto.p2: Interaction stays in the browser: sorting, grading and slider drags send no requests. When the model is needed, one action event returns to the conversation.
manifesto.mech1Body: The model writes dsh-ui JSON from a fixed vocabulary.
manifesto.mech2Body: The host validates and repairs the spec; the client draws the components.
manifesto.mech3Body: User actions go back to the conversation as action events.
surfaces.lede: One answer, three surfaces. Scroll to watch it change.
surfaces.step1Body: All a model could give before
surfaces.step3Body: Readings, range and trend at a glance
surfaces.caption: Rendered live — not a screenshot
surfaces.textP1: 18 tasks shipped this week, 2 slipped, average cycle 3.4 days. Frontend 8, backend 6, design 4. Payments integration slipped two days — the week's only risk.
surfaces.textP2: No sortable columns, no draggable chart, no quiz that grades itself.

action.lede: Buttons, submissions and sorting are local state. When the model is needed, a named event returns to the conversation.
action.step1: The reader clicks a button that carries an action
action.step2: The event is queued; local state updates first
action.step3: The model reads the event in a new turn
action.step4: A new interface replaces the old one
action.payloadNote: The action name comes from the spec. The host sends it back as an ordinary user message — no extra wrapper.
evidence.title: Check it yourself.
evidence.lede: The repository holds the recording, tests and a compatibility matrix. Each item below points at a file you can check.
aria-label:evidence.videoAria: Recording of dsh-genui in a real DSH session
evidence.videoCaption: Original repo recording · real DSH session · 53 s
evidence.compatBody: Declared in package.json peerDependencies. npm latest is 0.15.0; this site renders from the main-branch renderer, so it shows one version ahead.
evidence.testsBody: 152 spec files covering spec validation, streaming, focus and URL policy.
evidence.exportBody: Node count, nesting depth and panel size are hard-capped; media URLs accept only http(s) and same-origin relative paths.
install.lede: Then ask for a dsh-ui fence in any conversation — or just say “draw it with GenUI”.
install.footNote: Restart the web host after install; fences work immediately.

action.payloadText: [genui-action] refresh. The user just triggered this action "refresh" in the interface. Carry it out using the component data, then reply with an updated dsh-ui fence. Component data: {"type":"button","label":"Refresh data"}
atlas.composeNote: The same vocabulary, composed into one real answer
